issue.title: Bound agent.cleanup requests that serialize the entire fleet corpus
issue.description: PROPOSED BY sase-zn.4 note 1; independently reproduced by sase-zn.land on 2026-09-12 at e498ce822, after proc runtime retention landed. Of 121 retained operation-request.json files, eight exceed 1 MiB; the largest is 12,931,369 bytes. Its agent.cleanup payload carries 7,418,714 bytes of compact-JSON agents_with_children and 1,978,823 bytes of dismissed_identities. The source serializes the complete in-memory corpus in _kill_procs.py and related cleanup producers, then ops/commands/agent.py rehydrates it. This is pre-existing durable argv producer behavior (0835b38d2), not subprocess stdout. Design a bounded cleanup request that preserves family/related-agent resolution, transaction recovery, and dismissal correctness without copying the entire unrelated fleet and dismissed corpus for one action. Runtime retention is already covered by sase-zw.3/e498ce822; preserve it and do not duplicate it. Shared planning/selection and wire behavior belong in Rust. Size large because request ownership, compatibility, and replay need a design pass. All-status task searches, recent-task sweep, and active epic review found no duplicate payload-minimization owner.

task_type_fields.impact: Each cleanup copies and persists megabytes of unrelated fleet state, adding synchronous preparation work and avoidable allocation/disk cost despite bounded stdout and runtime retention.
task_type_fields.repro: Read-only: enumerate ~/.sase/procs/runtime/*/operation-request.json by stat size and inspect only operation and serialized field lengths. The audit found agent.cleanup at 12,931,369 bytes with agents_with_children 7,418,714 bytes and dismissed_identities 1,978,823 bytes. In an isolated large-fleet fixture, submitting a single-agent cleanup serializes the whole supplied fleet.
